proposed.explanation:
Your premise is the reverse of what the evidence shows. The FY2025 consolidated statement reports net profit of 82,258,815,000 EGP (≈ 82.3 billion) for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, versus 55,256,732,000 EGP (≈ 55.3 billion) for 31 Dec 2024. In other words, profit rose by roughly 49 % year-on-year, not fell by a third. The 55-billion figure you saw is the 2024 number, not the 2025 one. Supporting this, basic EPS grew from 14.72 EGP to 18.25 EGP (+24 %), and net interest income expanded from about 91.1 billion to 107.7 billion EGP (+18 %).

Given that your stated goal is to keep or add to your CIB position, your 5-year horizon, and the fact that the evidence points to earnings growth rather than decline, there is no basis in the provided data to sell. I would recommend holding your 400 COMI shares.

I am not recommending a buy here because your portfolio currently consists solely of COMI (400 × 128 = 51,200 EGP) plus 20,000 EGP cash, making COMI about 72 % of total portfolio value. The diversification rule caps any single company at 50 % of portfolio value after a purchase, so adding even one more share would breach that limit. You would need to diversify into other holdings before you could responsibly add to COMI.

Risks and caveats: the evidence covers only one fiscal year's income-statement line items; it does not include balance-sheet data, loan-quality metrics, capital adequacy, or the macro/interest-rate environment that drives a bank's earnings. A single year of profit growth does not guarantee continued growth over your 5-year horizon. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

limitations: Evidence is limited to income-statement line items (net profit, EPS, net interest income) for two fiscal years; no balance-sheet, credit-quality, capital-adequacy, or forward-looking data is provided.
A single year of profit growth does not assure continued growth over a 5-year horizon; macro, regulatory, and competitive risks are not captured in the evidence.
The investor's portfolio is 100 % concentrated in one stock, which is a structural risk independent of CIB's fundamentals.
